title: [F1-S7] Decide privileged-workflow executable-closure policy
body:
## Plan link

[Factory plan D112-D113](https://github.com/syamaner/roastpilot-plan/blob/main/roastpilot-cloud/factory.md#d112-23-jul-2026--constrain-local-actions-to-the-protected-audit-root), F1-S7.

Refs #10. Depends on #114 / D112-D113.

## Context

Draft Codex review of #114 / PR #119 identified a valid residual risk after direct local-action entrypoints are confined: a protected Node entrypoint can dynamically import, require, or spawn mutable workspace code outside `.github/**`. The same class is broader than Node imports:

- composite actions can execute arbitrary workspace paths through shell `run` steps;
- container actions can access the mounted workspace at runtime;
- privileged workflow `run` steps can intentionally execute mutable application code;
- an import-graph-only check cannot prove a dynamic runtime closure.

The current policy is path/classification based: factory implementing-agent patches cannot modify `.github/**`, `scripts/factory/**`, CODEOWNERS, or classified privileged glue. It does not currently promise a transitive closure of every instruction executed by CI. The repository has no local actions today, so this is latent, but the policy must be decided before a repository-local action is introduced into a privileged factory job.

Independent PR triage classified this `medium` / P2 residual and real-but-follow-up. D113 explicitly excludes import-graph and shell-command tracing from #114.

## Decision needed

Choose and record one enforceable policy across Node, composite, container, and ordinary privileged workflow commands:

1. **Forbid repository-local actions in privileged jobs** and require privileged commands to use explicitly classified/protected glue paths. Recommended for tractability.
2. Define a verifiable immutable/self-contained artifact contract with provenance for every privileged executable dependency.
3. Explicitly accept human-reviewed delegation from protected workflow/action code to mutable workspace code, documenting the residual trust boundary.

Do not choose a Node-import-only scan: it would leave sibling execution mechanisms open and violate D104's fix-the-class rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inventory every write-token or secret-bearing factory job and the repository code paths it can execute.
- [ ] Record the operator-approved executable-closure policy as the next plan decision.
- [ ] Apply the decision consistently to Node imports/spawns, composite shell steps, container workspace access, and ordinary privileged `run:` steps.
- [ ] Define the protected-path/classification consequences and failure behavior.
- [ ] Decompose enforcement into an ordered set of thin PRs, each under 400 logic lines, with factory-security and QA routing.
- [ ] Add adversarial acceptance cases for each relevant execution mechanism.
- [ ] Keep repository-local actions out of privileged factory jobs until this decision is resolved.

## In-scope surface

Factory plan and threat model; privileged workflow/job inventory; protected glue classification; any later enforcement design and adversarial tests.

## Out of scope

No implementation belongs in this decision issue until the operator selects a policy and a thin PR plan is recorded. #114 remains responsible only for the D112-D113 local-reference, manifest, and direct runner-entrypoint boundary.

## Verification notes

The decision brief must cite the live workflow/glue inventory and demonstrate how the chosen rule handles all four execution classes above. Any implementation slices require `factory-security-reviewer` and QA before opening.

## Size declaration

Larger architecture decision requiring decomposition after policy selection.

## Domain reviewer

`factory-security-reviewer` + QA; product/PM decision required first.
